stories.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Week 2's top 10 scorers through Sunday's late slate
stories.summary: An updated list of the top 10 fantasy scoring leaders in Week 2 through Sunday's late slate.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 20: Week 2's scoring leaders through Sunday's 4 p.m. ET games

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks - 42.5
Josh Allen, QB, Buffalo Bills - 40.82
CeeDee Lamb, WR, Dallas Cowboys - 35.3
Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR, Detroit Lions - 35.2
Jared Goff, QB, Detroit Lions - 29.8
Dak Prescott, QB, Dallas Cowboys - 29.76
Brock Purdy, QB, San Francisco 49ers - 28.48
DeVonta Smith, WR, Philadelphia Eagles - 27.7
Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals - 26.5
Dalton Schultz, TE, Houston Texans - 26.0

Check out the complete list of scoring leaders here.

Sept. 18: Josh Allen puts league on notice with 40-point night
by Adam Rank

We had one of the highest-scoring Week 1s in NFL history last week. There was no way we could possibly top that, yeah? Well, I've got news for you, the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions accepted the challenge and put up massive numbers on Thursday night.

Josh Allen led the way with more than 40 points to get your week started. We went into the draft season saying Allen was in his own tier and he's proving it early on. Allen had over 300 total yards and five total touchdowns. Allen is the third player in NFL history with nine total touchdowns and no turnovers in his team's first two games of the season. The other two were Patrick Mahomes in 2018 and Peyton Manning in 2013. Both went on to win MVP. Manning's Broncos also set the NFL record for most points in the season.

The Bills are the first team to record 35 points and more than 400 yards of offense in both of their first two games of the season since the Packers in 2020. The Bills have also scored five touchdowns in five red zone drives.
My guy Tristan H. Cockcroft pointed out during our in-game group chat that Allen broke the record for most fantasy points scored in the first two weeks of the season. Breaking the record of ... Ryan Fitzpatrick, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers version (as noted by Field Yates, who knew the answer to Tristan's trivia question).
Our group chat also had an interesting conversation about James Cook III. Is he a trade-high candidate because it's Josh Allen's offense, including goal-line carries -- or do you try to get more shares of Cook, if possible? Put me in the convo for more shares. I want as much of this Bills offense as possible. Especially if D.J. Moore is going to miss time. (Note: Moore is considered day-to-day)
Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir both had six targets. Joshua Palmer had a 43-yard TD reception on his lone target.
Dalton Kincaid had seven receptions for 95 yards and one receiving touchdown. He now has 225 receiving yards this season -- the first Bills player to do that since Stefon Diggs in 2022. Maybe those Travis Kelce comparisons Kincaid had coming into the league might finally be happening.
I thought Jared Goff's preseason ranking was way too low, with him going in the teens. He has put up huge numbers in the first two games of the season. He might have to continue this pace when you consider the condition of the Lions' defense.
I had Amon-Ra St. Brown as my WR2 heading into the season. Did I have him too low? Nine receptions for 142 and a pair of touchdowns. His sixth career game with 100-plus receiving yards and two touchdowns. It's wild.
Jahmyr Gibbs had 100-plus scrimmage yards, six receptions and a touchdown. And yet, it feels like not enough when you look at some of the other gaudy numbers being thrown around on Thursday night.

Sept. 18: Notes from NFL Nation
NFL Nation reporters are on the ground at NFL stadiums, locker rooms and practice facilities. Here's what they're seeing and hearing.

Saints running backs: Travis Etienne and Kendre Miller each had nine carries against the Lions in Week 1. Now, with Alvin Kamara back in the fold, it would be wise to proceed cautiously with Etienne as an RB1.

The Saints haven't said how they'll utilize all three backs, although Etienne and Kamara will likely both be involved in the passing game. But expect some sort of split between at least two backs going forward, according to Saints coach Kellen Moore. "We've got to rotate all these running backs and there'll be different packages or responsibilities from week to week that are different, but I think it's important. I think really my one year in Philly is probably the only year I've ever been with where a running back just kind of takes everything until he can't. Everywhere else you need to rotate these guys," Moore said this week. --Katherine Terrell

Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase had just two catches on four targets in Week 1 against Tampa Bay. Cincinnati knows it will have to get him the ball more against Houston. "It's less of a balance and more of a 'We gotta get him involved,'" QB Joe Burrow said this week. "I think that sentiment was echoed from a lot of different fronts after the game, and you can't come out of a game like that and have Ja'Marr Chase touch the ball two times. That'll certainly be an emphasis."

Last season, Chase followed up a similar Week 1 performance against the Cleveland Browns -- two catches for 26 yards -- with 14 receptions, 165 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. -- Ben Baby

Commanders receiving corps: TE Chig Okonkwo is out for Sunday's game with a hamstring injury. Washington likes to use three receiver sets and will do so again Sunday with rookie WR Antonio Williams coming off a strong debut. Washington does not have another proven pass-catching tight end beyond Okonkwo. But it will provide an opportunity for 2024 second round pick Ben Sinnott, who has just 16 career receptions. -- John Keim

Sept. 17: Bills emphasize tight ends ahead of Thursday night game

By Michael F. Florio

The Bills will open their new stadium on Thursday and will be doing so with a new-look offense. In Week 1, they played 13 personnel (three tight ends) on 39% of their offensive plays. Last season, their high in any game was 16%, and they used it over 10% in only three games.

The Bills also aired the ball out more. Josh Allen averaged 12.6 air yards per attempt, highest than in any game in the last two seasons. It led to 34% of their passes being explosive (15-plus yards), a higher rate than in any game in 2025.

The new approach led to a career-high 130 yards for Dalton Kincaid, who played 77% of the snaps, more than in any game in 2025. DJ Moore had his first 100-yard game with a touchdown since Week 12 of 2024. Both are fantasy starters in Week 2.

More Week 1 trends

The 13 personnel is here to stay. In 2025, the Rams were the only team to use it more than 13% of the time. In Week 1, seven teams used it over that rate. That means fewer receiver snaps, making those high-end options more valuable.
The Packers threw more in Week 1. They passed on 69% of offensive plays, the third-highest mark in any of their games since 2024. Jordan Love attempted 42 passes, the fourth most of his career. Also, Christian Watson saw WR1 usage, setting new career highs in routes run (37) and yards after the catch (73). An unproven rushing attack could lead to career years for this duo.
Bhayshul Tuten led the Jaguars' backfield in opportunities in Week 1. The Jags were putting him in a position to use his speed as 12 of 18 chances were outside runs. Now he gets Denver, who allowed the most yards on outside runs in Week 1 to the speedy Kenneth Walker III.

Sept. 16: Aaron Jones' arrow points up as Vikings put Jordan Mason on IR

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

Well, that escalated quickly.

Jordan Mason, who emerged from Week 1 as a potential pickup/trade target, instead unexpectedly landed on injured reserve on Wednesday due to a thumb injury. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell had indicated on Monday that Mason exited Week 1 with thumb soreness and would have the injury evaluated, with the follow-up revealing a small fracture in the digit that required "fixing," per The Athletic's Alec Lewis.

An IR move rules Mason out for the next four games. His absence dramatically alters the Vikings' offensive game plan heading into Week 2, a game in which they might also be without starting quarterback Kyler Murray (concussion). After all, it was Mason's 28-yard run early in the fourth quarter that played a big part in the Vikings' drive that earned them a lead they wouldn't relinquish, and his explosiveness is noticeably greater than that of 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr.'s at this stage of his career.

Expect Jones to handle the majority of the Vikings' carries over the next four weeks, with DeeJay Dallas elevating to No. 2 on the depth chart, though Jones gets primarily an opportunity-based rankings bump rather than an endorsement to aggressively pursue him in trade talks. Dallas is more of a wait-and-see, likely a change-of-pace back who would need to earn close to an even split with Jones to warrant standard league relevance.

What I'd like to see is rookie sixth-rounder Demond Claiborne be activated for No. 3 status for Week 2, as he's the Vikings running back with intriguing upside. One of my "also" preseason deep sleeper picks, Claiborne is a worthwhile stash in deep redraft and all dynasty leagues (if available at all in the latter).

Sept. 16: Notes from NFL Nation
NFL Nation reporters are on the ground at NFL stadiums, locker rooms and practice facilities. Here's what they're seeing and hearing.

Broncos' run game issues: While they'll almost certainly muscle up a bit more in Week 2, consider this a caveat until the Denver Broncos show their hand with the run game a little more. Yes, they like their top three backs, they say they want to run the ball more (as they said all offseason) but then they had just six carries in the first half of Monday's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. J.K. Dobbins is still RB1, but they want to limit his mileage now so he can impact the offense in the second half of the season. Rookie Jonah Coleman will get some of those personnel groupings, while RJ Harvey will get first looks in the long-yardage situations and it will be a shock if he doesn't lead their RBs in receptions. But clarity on how all that looks may not be around the corner, so managers should take a wait-and-see approach until they prove they will actually hand their RBs the ball. -- Jeff Legwold

Wide receiver George Pickens had two drops in the season opener against the New York Giants, including one on a deep ball that may have gone for a long touchdown. Coach Brian Schottenheimer will not say anything to his receiver. "George will be just fine," Schottenheimer said. "He's going to usually catch that ball going down the sideline and probably pull through it and then jump over people and spin and then jump into the end zone. And so I don't worry about George." Pickens on if the drops vs. the Giants are motivating: "Most definitely. Always motivating. Even when you do good, you should be still motivated to do better. But definitely motivating."-- Todd Archer

Rashod Bateman is the wide receiver to watch for the Baltimore Ravens following injuries at the position. Zay Flowers, Baltimore's No. 1 wide receiver, didn't practice Wednesday because of a hamstring issue and is day-to-day, according to head coach Jesse Minter. Ja'Kobi Lane, the Ravens' No. 3 wide receiver, was placed on injured reserve after having wrist surgery and will be out for a month. Even though Bateman didn't record a catch in Week 1, Ravens QB Lamar Jackson said his relationship with him is great, saying, "My guy is actually going to get a lot more targets, I believe, with guys going down just because our offense is so explosive." -- Jamison Hensley

Wide receiver Malik Nabers looked "good" during a walk-through practice on Wednesday, according to coach John Harbaugh. It was notable to see how Nabers bounced back following his first game action since tearing the ACL in his right knee in Week 4 of last season. Nabers looked better as the game went on Sunday night, where he was targeted nine times and finished with six receptions for 69 yards. The Giants are expecting Nabers to get more comfortable and explosive by the week, eventually returning to form early this season as one of the league's best receivers. -- Jordan Raanan

Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker (ankle) was limited in practice Wednesday but shed the walking boot on his left foot. Coker was wearing the boot in the locker room on Monday after he said he rolled his left ankle in the first quarter of the 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears. He said at the time that he didn't expect to miss practice. And on Wednesday, with a heavily wrapped left foot, Coker was seen working off to the side with a trainer. He ran sprints at times during the media portion of practice. Coker caught eight passes for 138 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago, including a 51-yard score in the second quarter following the injury.

Washington Commanders TE Chig Okonkwo was not a participant at practice Wednesday due to a groin injury. Coach Dan Quinn said his status for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys is uncertain. -- John Keim

Sept. 16: Need a roster reset? The players you should be eyeing for your bench

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

Week 1 did not present the coziest circumstances for fantasy managers with roster shortcomings. These include those who had bad injury luck in the latter stages of the preseason, Vampire league managers and dynasty managers who went all-in for 2025 and have had to piece together their season-opening rosters, to name a few.

A record 12 players scored more than 30 fantasy points in Week 1. We saw the Chicago Bears' 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers, the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. When you're digging deeper into the player pool, it feels daunting keeping up with production like that.

If you're in a roster pinch -- as I am in my Vampire league as well as my big dynasty league where I burned 2026 resources to win last year -- the best advice I can give is to maximize absolutely every facet of your roster.

Convert those stale bench spots into high-ceiling players who might pop in the coming weeks. Home in on ideal weekly kickers and defense/special teams, where even a handful of bonus points at low cost can mean a world of difference in matchups. Stealing a game or two as you let your team simmer and angling for a transformation into a midseason freight train is the way to go.

If there's one Week 1 performer who most struck me as the player to stash, it's Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams. He caught all four of his passes, including a 1-yard touchdown with 1:01 to go, scoring 16.4 fantasy points. Though only fourth on the team's WR depth chart, Williams showed good speed (especially on a 33-yard, fourth-quarter catch) and had no problems breaking free from Philadelphia Eagles cornerbacks. Williams, a 2026 third-rounder, is one of the better candidates to pull a later-season rookie emergence, à la Luther Burden III a year ago.
For D/ST streamers, we got more strategic clarity regarding which offenses to stream against: It's the Cleveland Browns, then the Miami Dolphins, then the Tennessee Titans. The Browns scored 10 points and were sacked five times in Week 1, and even if they switch from Deshaun Watson, know that Browns opponents averaged 10.6 fantasy points in backup Shedeur Sanders' seven starts last season. While there will be some variability in Malik Willis' play, he's still sack- and interception-prone, which makes his team a top target. The Titans totaled a second-worst 195 yards, continuing the poor play and reports that surrounded Cam Ward's offense since the preseason. Get the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (47.3% rostered in ESPN leagues, vs. CLE), then the San Francisco 49ers (35.5%, vs. MIA), everywhere for Week 2.
One more D/ST note: The Cincinnati Bengals played much more inspiring defense under second-year coordinator Al Golden, sacking Baker Mayfield four times and generating four turnovers on their way to a position-leading 20 fantasy points. I'm not adding them in fantasy leagues yet, but the Bengals D/ST is suddenly on my streaming watch list for appealing Week 5 (@MIA), Week 8 (TEN) and Week 13 (@CLE) matchups.

Sept. 15: Walker puts up MVP effort in Chiefs debut

By Michael F. Florio

The story going into Monday night's game was about two QBs returning from injury. However, Super Bowl XL-winning running back Kenneth Walker III stole the show.

Walker, now with the Kansas City Chiefs, played 69% of snaps and turned 23 carries into a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown. He also added three catches for 18 yards and a touchdown on six targets. It is just the sixth time in his career that he saw six-plus targets in a game. In total, Walker finished with 34.1 fantasy points and was the RB2 in a high-scoring week that saw a record 12 players score at least 30.

Walker was the focal point of the Chiefs offense and more than looked the part. Those who drafted him as an RB1 should feel great after this one. Walker has the chance to be the top-scoring RB in Week 2 against the Indianapolis Colts, who allowed 129 yards on outside runs to RBs in Week 1, the second most behind only the Denver Broncos. Walker picked up 129 of his yards on outside runs.

Patrick Mahomes shook some rust off early, and while he still doesn't look 100%, he appears to be getting closer. Mahomes threw for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, adding 23 rushing yards and a touchdown on seven carries. He scored 21.66 fantasy points and was the QB9 on the week. That's not bad against a Broncos defense that historically has given Mahomes a tough time.

Bo Nix did not have nearly as encouraging a return. He threw for 131 yards, one touchdown, one interception and ran for two yards. He fumbled three times, but only lost one. The Broncos offense looked out of sync in their first game with new playcaller Davis Webb. Nix finished with just 5.44 fantasy points and can be benched next week against the Jacksonville Jaguars. We need to see better results before we can trust him.
Jaylen Waddle also struggled in his Broncos debut. He was targeted only three times, catching one pass for two yards. He did drop one that had the potential to be a nice catch-and-run play. It is far too early to panic, but the lack of volume in a game the Broncos never led is concerning. He is not a must-start option in 10-team leagues until we see otherwise.
Courtland Sutton led Broncos receivers in snaps but finished with just two catches for 11 yards on five targets. Sutton can be benched in 10- and 12-team leagues for the time being. Pat Bryant led the Broncos with six targets, catching four for 42 yards. He is worth grabbing off the waiver wire, but managers should not force him into their lineups. Tight end Evan Engram led the Broncos with 43 yards and scored their lone touchdown. He is just a deep-league option.
RJ Harvey led the Broncos backfield with 53% of snaps. He only saw three carries but was the passing-down back and had 14 routes and four targets. J.K. Dobbins played 40% of the snaps, tallying eight carries and no targets for 36 yards. The distribution of work seems clear, with Dobbins leading on the ground and Harvey through the air. That makes Dobbins the safer "floor play," while Harvey has more upside. Neither is more than a flex option.
It was not a huge day for the Chiefs' pass catchers. Travis Kelce led the way with 71 yards on three catches (five targets). His day was made on a 59-yard catch-and-run. Rashee Rice scored a touchdown but only saw two targets for 19 yards. Xavier Worthy led the way with six targets but finished with three catches for 18 yards. Rice and Kelce are the only ones that should be started on a weekly basis.
Backup RB Emmett Johnson ran eight times for 24 yards and caught both his targets for 44 yards. He is a powerful runner that proved difficult to bring to the ground. While he likely does not see enough work to have standalone value, he is one of the top insurance backs in the game.

Sept. 14: Who got the ball on Sunday?

By Eric Moody

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals

Bucky Irving is still the lead back for the Buccaneers and finished with 15 touches and 20.3 fantasy points. Kenny Gainwell had six touches and wasn't too far behind in snaps, but Irving consistently handled the larger share. Gainwell's role is still too small to trust in fantasy. Additionally, we didn't learn much about the goal-line work. Sean Tucker was inactive, and Tampa Bay never had a goal-line snap.

New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions

Travis Etienne Jr.'s role was better than the carry totals make it look. Etienne and Kendre Miller each had nine rushing attempts, but Etienne played more snaps and was far more involved in the passing game. He drew eight targets and was regularly on the field when the Saints threw. Miller can take away some carries, but Etienne still has the more valuable fantasy role.

Juwan Johnson's usage was better than his seven targets and three catches suggest. He finished with more snaps and routes than Noah Fant. Fant saw more targets, but Johnson was more involved overall.

New York Jets at Tennessee Titans

Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are getting awfully close to a 50-50 split. Pollard handled more of the rushing work, but Spears played nearly the same number of snaps, ran far more routes and saw more targets. Both finished with 4.4 fantasy points. Spears is going to remain a significant part of this backfield.

Carnell Tate already looks like a major part of the Titans' offense, as he led the team's receivers in snaps and routes and tied for the lead in wide receiver targets.

Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers

Drake London led the Falcons' receivers in snaps, routes and targets, so the bigger issue was quarterback play, not usage. Kyle Pitts Sr. is more concerning after playing fewer snaps than you'd like, despite running a healthy number of routes, and drawing just one target. One game isn't enough to panic, but managers need to see more considering his ADP.

Pittsburgh's backfield is the epitome of a committee. Rico Dowdle played more snaps and ran far more routes, while Jaylen Warren had more rushing attempts and targets. It's a true situational split. Warren has the more attractive fantasy profile after finishing with 15 touches compared to Dowdle's 10, but neither back clearly separated.

DK Metcalf is clearly the Steelers' top receiver, but Roman Wilson caught my attention. Metcalf led the room in snaps, routes and targets (10). Michael Pittman Jr. played significant snaps, but Wilson drew twice as many targets. That's a usage trend I want to see again in Week 2.

Chicago Bears at Carolina Panthers

D'Andre Swift still leads this backfield, but Kyle Monangai is going to continue to be involved. Swift led the Bears' backs in snaps and touches (19), but Monangai stayed involved and finished with 12 touches of his own. Chicago also ran 70 offensive plays and scored 59 points, which won't happen every week, so there was more than enough work to go around. Swift remains a high-end RB2, but this isn't his backfield alone.

Don't let Colston Loveland's zero catches scare you. He was on the field far more than Cole Kmet and ran significantly more routes. The targets simply didn't come this week. I'd rather bet on that type of usage than chase a tight end who scored on a handful of routes.

Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan look more like 1A and 1B than WR1 and WR2. They played almost the same number of snaps, ran nearly the same number of routes and combined for 17 targets. Coker was the one who exploded with a career-best 33.8 fantasy points, but McMillan's role was still strong. Xavier Legette was clearly behind both.

Chuba Hubbard is still well ahead of Jonathon Brooks. Hubbard led the backfield in snaps, routes, touches and fantasy points. Brooks flashed with a 48-yard reception, but his role was nowhere close to Hubbard's. That could change as Brooks gets further removed from his long layoff, but right now Hubbard is the starter and Brooks is a stash.

Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars

Denzel Boston's role deserves attention. He led Browns receivers in snaps and routes and finished with 13.9 fantasy points. Jerry Jeudy and KC Concepcion were both involved, but Boston's playing time makes it hard to dismiss his Week 1 performance as a fluke.

Bhayshul Tuten's 15 rushing attempts make the Jaguars backfield look cleaner than it really was. Chris Rodriguez Jr. stayed involved, ran more routes and played a similar number of snaps. This isn't a one-man backfield yet.

Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans

Dalton Kincaid led the Bills tight ends in snaps, routes and targets and finished with 18 fantasy points. Buffalo still used multiple tight ends, but Kincaid was the one being featured as a receiver.

The Texans have a fairly even running back split when you look at snaps. David Montgomery handled most of the rushing attempts, while Woody Marks ran more routes. Montgomery is the early-down and short-yardage back and finished with 28.9 fantasy points thanks to three touchdowns. Marks is primarily used on passing downs. Montgomery remains the Texans back to roster and a solid RB2.

Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders

Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas have separated from the rest of the Dolphins receiver room. Washington drew eight targets and Douglas seven, while both played far more snaps than the other receivers. They're worth stashing if that usage continues.

Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings

Matthew Golden's role may be the biggest story in Green Bay, as he led the Packers in snaps, routes and targets. Christian Watson had the monster game with 32.7 fantasy points, but Golden's 12 targets are what I'd circle going forward. Green Bay has also consolidated its receiver rotation to Golden, Watson and Jayden Reed this year, which should make the group easier to navigate for managers.

MarShawn Lloyd is the Packers' lead runner, but Chris Brooks is still involved in the passing game. Lloyd handled 13 rushing attempts, while the two backs ran the same number of routes and weren't far apart in snaps. Lloyd has the better rushing role, but Brooks' receiving work makes Lloyd harder to trust as anything more than a flex.

Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles

Stefon Diggs' target volume jumped off the page. Terry McLaurin played more snaps and ran significantly more routes, but Diggs drew nine targets compared to McLaurin's four. The Commanders wanted the ball in Diggs' hands when he was on the field. That's an encouraging sign for Diggs' fantasy value.

Dontayvion Wicks played almost as many snaps as DeVonta Smith and ran nearly the same number of routes. He finished with four targets and 15.3 fantasy points, putting him firmly on the waiver wire radar this week.

Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers

Tyler Allgeier led the backfield in snaps, routes and rushing attempts (17), although Jeremiyah Love was more involved as a receiver and found the end zone. Love may eventually take over more of the workload, but Week 1 looked like a committee.

Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants

Isaiah Likely finished with eight targets and 27.8 fantasy points in his Giants debut, but the underlying usage was less impressive. The Giants used a three-man rotation at tight end, and Likely came off the field in single-tight-end formations and on some third downs. His playing time will be worth monitoring moving forward.

stories.headline: Sources: Higuain at center of refs union beef with MLS NEXT Pro
stories.summary: The union that represents MLS and USL referees, launched a scathing critique of MLS NEXT Pro over its handling of an incident in which a coach committed what it described as "two deliberate acts of physical abuse and sexism towards a female referee."
stories.body:
The Professional Soccer Referees Association (PSRA), the union that represents MLS and USL referees, launched a scathing critique of MLS NEXT Pro over its handling of an incident in which a coach of an MLS NEXT Pro team committed what it described as "two deliberate acts of physical abuse and sexism towards a female referee."

Multiple sources told ESPN that the coach in question is Columbus Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain.

In a social media post on BlueSky, which didn't reference Higuain by name, the PSRA said that the acts consisted of squeezing the hand of the official and refusing to let go after being told "three times to stop." The post added: "This physical intimidation was compounded by a demeaning, sexist remark to the official, 'Don't forget that this is a man's game.'"

Multiple sources told ESPN that the incident occurred during the postgame handshake immediately following Crew 2's Aug. 23 match against Huntsville City FC. Higuain received a red card for the incident.

MLS NEXT Pro conducted an investigation, which resulted in Higuain being suspended for two games and ordered to take part in restorative practice training. A source added that Higuain has begun but not yet completed the training and has already served the two-game suspension.

At issue for the PSRA is that the punishments weren't severe enough. In its social media post, the PSRA said that U.S. Soccer policy mandates a minimum three-game suspension for a "forceful grab" and that acts of discrimination also require a minimum three-game suspension.

"The League's response falls drastically short of the right message to the participants, the referees, and the public. It needs to be reevaluated," the PSRA's social media post read.

In a statement to ESPN, MLS NEXT Pro said the league "immediately investigated the reported incident between the head coach and the female official. It was determined that the coach's behavior violated League policies and warranted additional discipline beyond the red card that was issued in the moment. He served a two-game suspension and is required to participate in a multi-session restorative practices process, which is already underway. The program is intended to support the League's efforts to foster understanding, accountability, respect, and the restoration of relationships across the League. MLS NEXT Pro believes in the restorative approach. The League is confident in its process and the results."

The Crew also sent the following statement to ESPN: "The Crew actively collaborated with MLS NEXT Pro throughout the review process and fully accepted the additional discipline issued in accordance with league policies.

"Our Club is dedicated to growing the game by creating environments where everyone is welcome and supported on and off the pitch, which is founded upon our values of respect, inclusivity and prioritizing people and culture first. We condemn any action or notion that contradicts our mission of uniting and uplifting all communities and genders through the global game."

As for why a heavier punishment wasn't meted out, one source with knowledge of the league's thinking indicated that the league believes the minimum suspension spelled out in U.S. Soccer policies is a guideline and not mandatory.

The U.S. Soccer policy manual is explicit on the matter of penalties for assault toward referees. Policy 202-2 Section 2 of the U.S. Soccer Policy manual, dated May 2026, states that "All Professional League Members shall adopt and enforce policies prohibiting misconduct against referees that meet the following minimum criteria."

The policy goes on to state that, "Any player, coach, manager, club official, or league official who commits an intentional act of physical violence at or upon a referee ('Referee Assault') shall be suspended without pay for a period of at least six consecutive matches (the "Assault Suspension"). The Assault Suspension shall commence with the first match after which the individual has been found to have committed this act."

Assault is defined in the U.S. Soccer Policy manual as including, but not limited to: "striking, kicking, choking, grabbing or bodily running into a referee; spitting on a referee with ostensible intent to do so; kicking or throwing an object at an official that could inflict injury; or damaging the referee's uniform or personal property (e.g., car, uniform, or equipment)."

The manual also states that "The Professional League Member may not provide for a penalty shorter than the Assault Suspension but may provide for a longer suspension and/or a fine."

The U.S. Soccer Policy manual says the minimum suspension for referee abuse -- defined as "verbal and nonverbal communication which contains foul or abusive language and which implies or directly threatens physical harm; spewing a beverage on or spitting at a referee or the referee's personal property" -- is three games.

Caleb Pongratz of Spotrac was the first to report that Higuain was the coach involved in the incident.

stories.headline: Anderson tosses 7 shutout innings, Mariners beat Rockies 2-1 to avoid elimination
stories.summary: — Rookie Kade Anderson tossed seven shutout innings, Dominic Canzone drove in two runs, and the Seattle Mariners beat the Colorado Rockies 2-1 on Sunday to stave off elimination from playoff contention.
stories.body:
DENVER -- — Rookie Kade Anderson tossed seven shutout innings, Dominic Canzone drove in two runs, and the Seattle Mariners beat the Colorado Rockies 2-1 on Sunday to stave off elimination from playoff contention.


Anderson (2-2), in the longest of his six starts since making his major league debut Aug. 22 at the Chicago Cubs, followed his worst outing with his best. He gave up three hits, struck out a career-high seven and didn’t walk a batter.


His performance kept Seattle’s slim postseason hopes alive. The Mariners (73-83) gained a game on Texas in the AL West and avoided, temporarily, being eliminated from the AL wild-card race.


Mariners closer Andrés Muñoz left the game after walking TJ Rumfield with one out in the ninth. Muñoz bent over flexing his right arm after missing on a 98 mph fastball, bringing out the trainer. Manager Dan Wilson said Munoz’s issue was with his right knee He was replaced by Eduard Bazardo, who got the final two outs around a walk for his first save.


Colorado catcher Hunter Goodman hit his 39th homer off Muñoz.


Rockies starter Tomoyuki Sugano, who entered Sunday with a 7.41 ERA in three September starts, set down the first 10 batters before running into trouble in the fourth. He walked Randy Arozarena, and he scored from first on Canzone’s single to center.


Canzone gave Seattle a 2-0 lead with an RBI double in the sixth off of Ryan Feltner.


Colorado’s best scoring opportunity against Anderson was in the sixth inning when Jake McCarthy tripled with one out. Anderson got Connor Norby looking for the second out and struck out Goodman to end the inning.


Rockies third baseman Kyle Karros was a late scratch with back spasms.

stories.headline: Stocks up, stocks down: Hayden Young goes down in folklore; why Neale needs to get off
stories.summary: It was an epic prelim final weekend, with Hayden Young writing himself into Fremantle folklore and Will Ashcroft putting the Dockers on notice. But James Sicily deserves his fine. Here's whose stocks are up and down.
stories.body:
We just witnessed one of the greatest AFL preliminary final weekends of all time, with Fremantle coming from behind to beat Sydney and Brisbane snatching victory over Hawthorn in an all-time classic. Here's whose stocks are up and down.

Our footy experts cast their eye over the week's action to find out whose stocks are up -- whether it's a coaching masterstroke or a player having a blinder -- and whose are down.

Brisbane
Stocks up: Could Will Ashcroft be a three-time Norm Smith Medal winner in a few days' time? It's absolutely crazy to think the 22-year-old could have three flags and three Norms in his first four seasons in the AFL. Just let that sink in for a moment. He's a (late) September specialist, picking up 28 disposals, kicking a goal, gathering eight clearances, and tallying more than 500 metres gained. His final act was a beauty, too. With his side up by three points and just a handful of second left on the clock, he won the decisive centre bounce, strolled out of the middle and hit Kai Lohmann to put the result beyond doubt. And how about the celebration too? He kept sprinting past Lohmann, a very Papley-esque razz-up of the crowd and his teammates as they made a fourth successive Grand Final berth. A staggering effort from the Lions.

Stocks down: The Lions could be without two-time Brownlow Medallist and star midfielder Lachie Neale after he was banned for one week for his stupid, unneccessary gut punch on Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan on Saturday. The Lions have already said they'll challenge at the tribunal, but it'll be difficult to overturn given the AFL specifically said it would be cracking down on unnecessary hits off the ball; according to Jon Ralph, six players have been given a week off for similar incidents. Will the tribunal cave under the pressure of it being a Grand Final this week? Is it too harsh to miss a premiership decider for something so -- comparatively -- minor? People will argue that if it's a suspension in Round 10 it should be this week as week, but perhaps the bar to miss a Grand Final needs to be higher. Many questions are yet to be answered, and we're not sure the answers will be popular with everyone...

Fremantle

Stocks up: It took one quarter for the Dockers to claim their epic prelim final win and there were two genuine X-factors that helped provide the necessary spark that has carried them into a first Grand Final appearance since 2013. Well, for Hayden Young, it began after the three-quarter time siren, the classy left-footer nailing the goal of the night with a brutally-difficult set shot from the left boundary line on the 50 in a moment that in hindsight changed the game entirely. Then up stepped Shai Bolton. After just one disposal in the premiership quarter, he kicked two goals from eight touches in the final stanza, and had a direct goal assist as well. It's the class of these stars that set the two teams apart at the SCG.

Stocks down: Did it matter on the night? Probably not, but only because of the above names who dragged them over the line. Freo's key forward trio of Josh Treacy, Jye Amiss, and Patrick Voss were quiet again, registering just eight disposals between them in the first half on Friday night. By the end of the match they combined for two goals (two very good ones, it must be said), but they've just got to do more next week. By the way, the Dockers have won just three total quarters (out of 12) this entire finals series. They deserve to be where they are, but how well are they really going?

Hawthorn
Stocks up: Was that one of Josh Ward's best games as a Hawk? In a game dominated by, yes, the Wizard kicking six goals and looking like an absolute star, it's only fair to show some love to one of the more underappreciated Hawks. Ironically he'd possibly be one of the players to lose midfield rotations in favour of Zach Merrett should he make the move to Hawthorn, but Ward was wonderful on Saturday evening; 25 disposals, four direct goal assists, a game-high 16 contested possessions. And Watson, six goals in a preliminary final is a herculean effort. What's his ceiling? Is it crazy to say best small forward of all time?

Stocks down: For two leaders of the club, James Sicily and Tom Barrass acted embarrassingly on Saturday night after the heartbreaking loss to the Lions. After the siren sounded to bring curtains down on Hawthorn's season, Sicily and Barrass were seen verbally accosting umpire Hayden Meyer, who made the late controversial decision to penalise Jarman Impey for holding the ball in the Hawks' back 50, leading to the Lions' winning goal. The optics were terrible for club leaders, made to look worse when Hawthorn fans threw bottles and cans onto the MCG in protest for the controversial -- yet correct -- decision. It's fitting Sicily was fined $10,000 and Barrass $5,000; it's unacceptable behaviour that filters to lower levels and cannot be excused.

Sydney
Stocks up: Errol Gulden really couldn't have done much more for the Swans since he returned from injury. His final seven games? 41, 34, 39, 47, 41, 34, and 35 disposals. In a team that was understrength, he constantly used his elite endurance and run and carry to lift his side to a prelim and agonisingly short of another Grand Final. Logan McDonald was another who thrived as a deep forward target throughout September, leaving no doubt he can partner Charlie Curnow in 2027 to become one of the league's best key forward duos. McDonald, after kicking six against Harris Andrews and the Lions in a qualifying final, was Sydney's highest-rated player on the ground against the Dockers, kicking three goals and taking four marks to go with 14 disposals and seven score involvements.

Stocks down: It was a valiant effort from the Swans on Friday night. Despite having the week off, they were undermanned and seemed to just run out of gas in the last quarter as the Dockers forced a late onslaught of inside 50s and threatening attacks. You must wonder where that leaves members of the 'Pullman Five' within the playing group. Would the additions of Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, and Nick Blakey (at the very least) have been the difference? Maybe. But who is to say if they had played, the Swans would have lost by more. It's speculation, but leaving 'what ifs' on the table really hurts -- just look at the emotions spilling out of stand-in skipper Dane Rampe, whose career may have come to an end with that loss.

stories.headline: Raptors honor Kyle Lowry with golden 'GROAT' statue
stories.summary: Lowry also received a key to the city of Toronto and a special dinner to honor his contribution to the franchise.
stories.body:
With a sea of red, white and black Kyle Lowry jerseys filling the streets of Toronto for an honorary block party, the guard's legacy will forever be stamped in the city's lore with an exclusive commemorative figure.

On Saturday, the Toronto Raptors honored Lowry's career with a block party outside of Scotiabank Arena, unveiling a golden raptor statue. The sculpture features Lowry's No. 7 jersey while dribbling a basketball and stands on a nameplate that reads "The Greatest Raptor of All Time. Kyle Lowry | 2012-2021, 2026."

The statue unveiling follows the franchise's August announcement that it would retire Lowry's jersey number during the upcoming 2026-27 season. It will be raised to the rafters at the conclusion of Toronto's home matchup against the Philadelphia 76ers on Jan. 10.

Along with the statue, the six-time All-Star received a key to the city.

"I've been looking forward to this moment for years. I always said that Toronto is home, and that I'd retire a Raptor, and to see my No. 7 go up in that building is going to mean everything to me," Lowry said. "We built something special here -- my teammates, the organization, the city and the fans, and all of Canada. We became champions together, and to be able to share this night with all of them, and with my family, is going to mean a lot to me."

Lowry, who spent nine of his 20 seasons in Toronto, helped bring the Raptors their only NBA championship in the 2019 NBA Finals. He will also join Basketball Hall of Famer Vince Carter as the only Raptors to have their numbers retired -- Carter's was retired in November 2024.

The 40-year-old Lowry announced his retirement in July after signing a one-day contract with Toronto to retire as a member of the franchise.

He averaged 13.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and six assists in his 20 seasons.

stories.headline: UFC 331 takeaways: Are we living in the greatest era for lightweights?
stories.summary: Arman Tsarukyan and Joshua Van stole the show with emphatic statements at UFC 331.
stories.body:
The main card of UFC 331 had shocking moments on top of shocking moments on top of pound-for-pound resume building.

First, Sean Sharaf got his first UFC win as the biggest underdog in the promotion's history against Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson in just 12 seconds. Then Arman Tsarukyan stepped into the cage for the first time this year and reminded everyone why the current crop of UFC lightweights may be the best ever. And flyweight champion Joshua Van followed it all up with a performance that should place him among the 10 best MMA fighters in the world right now. What more could an MMA fan want?

Van is a top five pound-for-pound fighter
I can't believe I'm saying this -- not because Van isn't great or hasn't been great for some time. It's just -- how does one become a top-five fighter in the world at age 24, with less than five years of pro experience?

After his performance on Saturday, I can't talk about Van anymore as just a phenom or a young champion. He is legitimately as good as just about anyone in the entire sport. Alexandre Pantoja coming off injury looked like the same Pantoja as before the injury. If anything, he looked even more determined than before. His pressure was appropriate and his decision-making was sound. Van was just better.

He defended takedowns and escaped on the ground when Pantoja could get him there. At one point, was it just me or did Van catch Pantoja's glove as he threw a punch, before countering? He caught some of Pantoja's kicks, in the same way he caught the one in December that led to Pantoja's injury. In the fifth round, when the result of the fight still felt up in the air, Van delivered his best five minutes of work, dropping Pantoja with a right hand.

Van is gifted athletically, confident and a natural finisher. He's been all of that from the first moment we saw him. One description that shouldn't be forgotten, however, is that he's extremely technical. This was one of the most technical fights of the entire year, against one of the best flyweights of all time, and Van ended up running away on the scorecards. If Van were 28, I don't think anyone would have an issue ranking him near the top of the pound-for-pound. The only hesitancy to do it is because -- it doesn't seem right or possible, given his age and relative inexperience. I'm getting over that. Van is top five. -- Brett Okamoto

Are we living in the greatest lightweight era of all time?

The history of the UFC's lightweight division is so undeniably rich. One of the division's greatest "eras" was from 2016 to 2020, when Conor McGregor became double champ at Madison Square Garden, Khabib Nurmagomedov dominated and timeless fighters such as Tony Ferguson, Dustin Poirier and Justin Gaethje were in their primes.

This upcoming chapter at lightweight has a chance to challenge all that.

Within the past three months, Ilia Topuria has suffered his first loss (in spectacular fashion to Gaethje on the White House lawn) and vowed revenge. Paddy Pimblett has turned in a star-making performance, submitting Benoît Saint Denis in less than a minute on a McGregor-headlined card. And now Arman Tsarukyan has completed an unbelievable walkoff knockout of Mauricio Ruffy. Topuria, Pimblett and Tsarukyan are three legitimate superstar storylines, and it just so happens they are all rivals who have promised to take each other out.

Don't forget that the champion, Gaethje, could postpone retirement in order to defend his throne. Veterans Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira are still active in the top five, too. Australia's Quillan Salkilld has had a breakout year, and Nurmagomedov's younger cousin, Usman, could potentially transition to the UFC after years of dominance in the PFL.

Yeah. The next few years could be the best in lightweight history, and that is really, really saying something. -- Okamoto

The Steveson train has hit an early crossroads

It's not like Steveson had never lost before. On his way to becoming a 2020 Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was formidable but not perfect. His record at the University of Minnesota was 103-3. His international freestyle record, including cadet and junior levels, was 53-2. Even an all-time great has had to pick himself up and dust himself off at times.

But this defeat was different from whatever Steveson had ever experienced. He got knocked out cold in 12 seconds by Sharaf, a guy who came into their fight 0-2 in the UFC with both losses coming by knockout. Let's just acknowledge that this matchmaking was a setup to build an MMA résumé for Steveson. Considering that he had just four pro fights under his belt, though, this was an appropriate booking.

The result was a shocker. It was the largest known upset in UFC history, per DraftKings. But what's done is done, and the story now takes an unexpected twist. Will this be just a speed bump on Steveson's express road toward the top of the UFC heavyweight division? Or will this defeat make Steveson timid in standup fighting, slowing his development beyond being a one-dimensional wrestler? Heavy-handed UFC heavyweights will surely be emboldened by seeing Steveson crash to the canvas. What seemed like a sure thing now is surrounded by question marks. The future might still be bright for Steveson. It probably will be. Here's a suggestion for Steveson: Don't bother watching the 12-second KO loss. Why put yourself through that again? Instead, go find video of Islam Makhachev's 2015 KO loss in his second UFC fight, then contemplate how Makhachev has managed to win all 17 of his fights since on his way to becoming the best pound-for-pound fighter in the sport. -- Jeff Wagenheim

stories.body:
Formula 1 is heading to the streets of Baku for this year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix as we roll into the business end of the season.

Title leader Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the drivers' championship after picking up his eighth victory of the season at the brand-new Madring last time out.

He leads his teammate George Russell by 81 points, with Lewis Hamilton now dropping back in the title race after a retirement in Spain.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 15th race of the season.

- Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Azerbaijan Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Thursday, September 24

Practice One: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Friday, September 25

Final Practice: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Azerbaijan Grand Prix: 12 p.m.

How to watch

Sky Sports has exclusive F1 rights again in 2026 in the U.K., with every session live on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the race on a Saturday?
For the first time in Baku's history, the F1 weekend will shift a day forwards, with the race taking place on a Saturday to avoid a clash with an Azerbaijan National Day of mourning on the Sunday.

Azerbaijan's people will dedicate their thoughts to military personnel and those who died during the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War.

Baku City Circuit

After the European leg of the calendar where circuits are more traditional, Baku is one of the standout street circuits of the season.

The first race in Baku was held in 2016 as the European Grand Prix before it was called the Azerbaijan Grand Prix a year later.

The section around Turns 8, 9 and 10 are lined by the walls of the city's charming old town including a castle and the long main straight along the Baku shoreline sees cars reach speeds in excess of 220 mph and is the best spot for overtaking.

The walls are narrow and the high-speeds make for either a race full of chaos, or none at all. There is a 57% chance of a Safety Car being deployed during the race.

Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Circuit: Baku City Circuit; Baku, Azerbaijan

Previous winners
2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes)

2021: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2022: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2023: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2024: Oscar Piastri (McLaren)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2016 European GP. (First race as Azerbaijan GP in 2017)

Laps: 51 laps of 6km.

Lap record: 1:43.009, Charles Leclerc (2019).

Most wins: Pérez (2021, 2023) and Verstappen (2022, 2025) with two wins each. Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2018), Bottas (2019) and Piastri (2024).

Most poles: Leclerc with four (2021-2024) and Hamilton (2017), Bottas (2019) and Verstappen (2025) are the other pole sitters from the current grid.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be dry and sunny throughout the weekend. Temperatures will be around 26°C, but will drop to 24°C for the race on Saturday.

What happened last year?
Red Bull's Verstappen took pole position around the streets of Baku in a qualifying session that featured a record six red flags.

He ended up converting that pole into a dominant victory, with Russell in second and Carlos Sainz behind.

It was a key moment in the championship fight between Lando Norris and Piastri as Norris closed the gap to 25 points to his McLaren teammate after the Australian crashed out.

Who will win this year?

The last street circuit this year was in Monaco in June and since then several of the top teams have upgraded its packages and haven't yet gone racing on street circuits, but Baku has now arrived.

Antonelli has looked on fire in the last two races, but Norris is creeping to the front. The reigning world champion has two wins to his name in Hungary and Zandvoort, but also suffered an unlucky run in Madrid with the safety car deployment, so missed out on a potential win there as well.

Mercedes are set to be quick in the high-speed straight lines in Baku, but the tight and twisty corners might suit Ferrari and McLaren best.

One of the main aims will be to not crash the car into the wall otherwise the whole course of the race can rapidly change in a blink of an eye.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: 'We're not done': Ponga, Knights plot Penrith upset
stories.summary: Kalyn Ponga has declared there are more chapters to write in Newcastle's revival story as the 2025 wooden spooners aim to upset Penrith to make the grand final.
stories.body:
Kalyn Ponga insists now is not the time for nostalgia as Newcastle's captain aims to move a step closer to completing one of the great NRL revivals by taking the Knights to the grand final.

After Sunday's drama-charged 12-10 win over the Warriors in Auckland, Newcastle's Cinderella finals run will extend into another week with Justin Holbrook's set to face Penrith in a preliminary final at Accor Stadium.

Fullback Ponga will feature after he passed the head injury assessment which left him watching the dying stages of the win over the Warriors from the dressing room.

Victory over the Panthers this Sunday would count as the Knights' biggest scalp to date and would cap the club's remarkable turnaround from wooden spooners to grand finalists in the space of 12 months.

The Roosters were the last side to finish last (2009) and reach the decider the following year.

But captain Ponga claims he has no desire to look back on the Knights' rapid progress under first-year Newcastle coach Holbrook as he believes there are more chapters to write.

"It's kind of hard right now because you're obviously grateful for the win but then you don't want to sit in that for too long," Ponga said.

"You want to get your mind to the next game, and that's been our strength this year.

"I think when it's all said and done, when we're sitting at home in the off season, I'll look back and be pretty proud of this season.

"But it's kind of hard right now because we're not done.

"All I do know is I'm really proud of this group for the efforts that they've put in throughout the whole year. I don't want to reflect too much just yet."

The Knights had the luxury of giving representative forward Dylan Lucas a cameo in the final 20 minutes of the win in Auckland and his return from injury will be a major boost for a side that has stumbled into September without a handful of big hitters.

Newcastle have survived into week three without their first-choice front-row duo of Jacob Saifiti and Trey Mooney and have thrived in attack despite the absence of injured star playmaker Dylan Brown.

"The belief sort of comes from the year. You go into these games relying on what you've done throughout the year," Ponga said.

"So many times we've had injuries, had to overcome adversity and challenges, and as a playing group, we've handled that pretty well. No doubt it'll be the same next week."

stories.headline: Lions to challenge Lachie Neale's AFL Grand Final ban
stories.summary: Brisbane will challenge Lachie Neale's one-match ban at the AFL tribunal in a bid to free the star midfielder to play in the Grand Final against Fremantle.
stories.body:
Brisbane Lions superstar Lachie Neale may attempt to lean on the "exemplary record" clause to clear himself for the AFL Grand Final against Fremantle after he was handed a one-match suspension.

Neale was offered the ban over the gut punch that floored Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan behind play during the Lions' nine-point win in an epic preliminary final on Saturday night.

The incident was graded intentional conduct, medium impact and body contact.

Within minutes of the AFL releasing the match review findings on Sunday, Brisbane confirmed they will challenge the ban.

Vision shows Ginnivan wrestling with Brisbane forward Eric Hipwood, before Neale jogs over and hits the Hawthorn player with a left-handed punch to the stomach.

Adelaide forward Riley Thilthorpe and Hawks pair James Sicily and Dylan Moore have all been suspended over similar incidents this season.

Those bans came after former Lions CEO Greg Swann - in his new role as AFL football boss - brought in a minimum one-match penalty for gut punches.

New match review guidelines state intentional strikes to the stomach are automatically graded as medium impact rather than low, resulting in one-match bans.

But Brisbane are almost certain to try their luck at the tribunal as doubt over Neale's availability dominates headlines entering Grand Final week.

Neale has never been suspended in his 320-game career and could use the same clause that helped games record-holder Scott Pendlebury escape suspension for his bump on Adelaide's Josh Worrell this season.

Under AFL regulations, "a player with an exemplary record may argue that their good record constitutes exceptional and compelling circumstances".

Players can no longer use the so-called "good bloke" defence that helped Brisbane's Charlie Cameron overturn a ban in 2024.

Neale's other option is to attempt to have the impact grading reduced, though that route would be unlikely to be successful.

If Neale's ban stands, it would mean he not only misses the premiership decider against his former club, but could also have played his last game for the Lions.

The 33-year-old two-time flag star is widely expected to join Collingwood as a free agent in the off-season.

Neale is no stranger to Grand Final week drama, after his calf injury was the major talking point ahead of last year's decider against Geelong.

The brilliant midfielder ultimately played as the substitute - under a system that has since been thrown out - and starred with 17 disposals and one goal to help the Lions secure back-to-back flags.

Neale wasn't the only player under match review scrutiny after Saturday's preliminary final.

Hawthorn defenders Sicily ($10,000) and Tom Barrass ($5000) were handed massive fines for misconduct after they had angry words with umpire Hayden Meyer immediately after the final siren.

It followed a controversial finish, in which a holding-the-ball free paid against Hawthorn's Jarman Impey gifted Brisbane's Hugh McCluggage the go-ahead goal in the dying stages.

The league determined the fixed financial sanction for abusive language towards an umpire was inadequate, and so charged Sicily and Barrass under the "other misconduct'' provision.

Hawks midfielder Jai Newcombe was cleared over his first-quarter contact with Neale in a collision that involved opponents pushing the two players into each other.

stories.body:
Michael Carrick played down concerns that Manchester United's poor start to the season has been caused by a lack of fitness within the squad.

United needed an 89th minute equaliser from Matheus Cunha to salvage a 1-1 draw with Fulham at Craven Cottage on Sunday after Lisandro Martínez knocked the ball into his own net to stake the hosts with a lead.

Afterwards, Cunha said Fulham's players "put in more energy" at the start of the second half before taking the lead.

But Carrick insisted fitness is not an issue, despite data from the game showing that Fulham's players covered an extra 6km.

"It didn't look like that to me," Carrick said after being asked about Cunha's assessment. "I was quite happy with the way we finished the game. I thought we finished the game really strongly actually and we kept pushing.

"So I don't think that's an issue, no."

The draw at Fulham leaves United on five points after five games -- their worst start to a Premier League season since 2014 -- and in 12th place in the standings.

Carrick admitted the start to the campaign is "not ideal," but praised his players for finding a way back at Craven Cottage when it looked like United would suffer a third damaging defeat in a week after exiting the Carabao Cup at the hands of Brighton on Wednesday.

"That's a big thing, without getting carried away with it, because we've taken a point and we wanted to win, but it's part of learning as a group," said Carrick. "How we respond, what it looks like moving forward, what our reaction is, all that. That's part of growing as a group.

"Definitely today it could have gone in a different direction -- 100% it could have. I was really pleased with the response and I think that'll help us a lot moving forward."

United not head into an extended break for the FIFA international window and do not play again until a home match against Tottenham Hotspur on Oct. 10.

stories.headline: UFC 331 results: Van dominates Pantoja to retain men's flyweight title
stories.summary: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan earned big wins on a contender for fight card of the year. Here are the UFC 331 highlights.
stories.body:
If there were any doubts about Joshua Van's championship mettle, they were put to bed after his dominant victory over Alexandre Pantoja in the UFC 331 main event at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Saturday night.

Van outstruck Pantoja and successfully defended double-digit takedown attempts and even dropped Pantoja in Round 5 en route to a unanimous decision win to retain the UFC men's flyweight title over the former champion.

Pantoja put up a good fight, as he held his own on the feet and racked up nearly 10 minutes of control time. His best showings were in Rounds 1 and 4, when he got a hold of Van and successfully took the fight to the mat. But Van did enough to get a win on the judges' scorecards. He has now defended his title twice.

In the co-main event, Arman Tsarukyan earned what could be the biggest win of his career, putting knockout artist Mauricio Ruffy to sleep with an elbow in Round 1. The win likely cements Tsarukyan as the top contender for UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.

Also on the main card, heavyweight Sean Sharaf pulled off an all-time UFC upset, knocking out top prospect Gable Steveson in just 12 seconds.

Brett Okamoto, Jeff Wagenheim and Dre Waters break down all the action from Los Angeles.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton shuts down asking Ferrari to make changes: 'Never asked for anyone to be replaced'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eight world championship is over.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eighth world championship is over.

Hamilton threw in the title towel at last weekend's Spanish Grand Prix after he retired from the race in Madrid with a brake problem.

His failure to finish leaves him 101 points behind Kimi Antonelli in the championship standings -- the equivalent of more than four victories -- with just nine scheduled rounds left.

A report in Italy claimed Hamilton has challenged Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur to make changes to the team's trackside staff.

But in a story posted to his Instagram account on Thursday, the 41-year-old wrote: "I've seen some of the stories that have gone out and I want to clear it up on here.

"I've never asked for anyone on my team to be replaced. Everyone I work with works hard every day, and their dedication is what moves us forward.

"I always try to empower and lift people to be the best versions of themselves or at least see the best in themselves.

"I may not always achieve that but it's my intention and what I'm here to do. We all work together and that will continue."

- Lando Norris backs 'exciting' 2027 Monaco GP sprint weekend but 'tougher for us drivers'

- Max vs 100: Verstappen jokes taking on '200' drivers next time after winning crazy challenge

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Hamilton sparked hope of challenging Antonelli -- the driver who replaced him at Mercedes -- when he won in Barcelona in June.

However, the British driver has not finished on the podium at the past five rounds and has been openly critical of his team's race tactics.

He also took aim at teammate Charles Leclerc's driving after an opening-lap clash in Monza earlier this month. Hamilton said he led face-to-face talks with the Monegasque to clear the air.

His retirement in Madrid marked his first of the campaign, and when asked to assess his title chances, Hamilton replied: "There's no stopping him [Antonelli] and Mercedes this year. They've done a phenomenal job, and they deserve it [the championship]."

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: What We Learned: Newcastle's kids are made for finals; Wahs have themselves to blame
stories.summary: The Knights shocked the Warriors in front of a packed Eden Park crowd on Sunday, sendign the Wahs packing from the finals, while Newcastle have set up a preliminary final clash with Penrith.
stories.body:
AUCKLAND, New Zealand -- The Newcastle Knights have silenced a sold-out Eden Park and kept their remarkable NRL finals run alive with a gripping 12-10 victory over the New Zealand Warriors.

Leka Halasima crossed twice for the hosts, but tries to Fletcher Sharpe and Dominic Young -- both converted by Sandon Smith -- proved enough for Newcastle to book a preliminary final showdown with the Penrith Panthers.

Here are three things we learned from Sunday's semifinal.

Newcastle's kids are made for September
The Knights arrived in Auckland with the youngest halves combination remaining in the competition and a forward pack missing several established names.

None of that mattered.

Fletcher Sharpe and Sandon Smith looked anything but overwhelmed by the occasion, calmly guiding Newcastle through a hostile afternoon in front of a deafening Eden Park crowd.

Sharpe's first-half try captured exactly what he offers this side. After Bradman Best stepped, fended and burst into the backfield, the five-eighth remained alive in support, juggled the pass and finished the movement to level the scores.

Smith was similarly composed. His two conversions ultimately provided the difference between the sides, with the young halfback refusing to allow the occasion -- or the noise surrounding him -- to alter his process.

The Knights' youngsters were just as impressive without the ball.

Newcastle repeatedly scrambled to survive Warriors raids, with Greg Marzhew producing two crucial interventions in the first half - knocking down a pass with a try looming before bundling Dallin Watene-Zelezniak into touch moments later.

Their defensive resolve became even more important as fatigue arrived and the Warriors threw everything at them late. The hosts enjoyed multiple attacking opportunities but Newcastle continually found a way to shut the door.

Kalyn Ponga did not need to manufacture every decisive moment himself. His early linebreaks and constant movement kept the Warriors' defensive line occupied, creating opportunities for Best, Sharpe and Newcastle's outside backs.

That might be the most encouraging sign of all for Justin Holbrook.

The Halasima gamble almost saved the Warriors' season

Leka Halasima entered the weekend under an injury cloud and was only confirmed in the Warriors' starting side shortly before kick-off.

He then came within inches of dragging their season into another week.

Used in the centres, the powerful youngster was comfortably New Zealand's most dangerous attacking player. His combination of footwork, strength and acceleration caused Newcastle problems from the opening exchanges.

Halasima struck first after 14 minutes, crashing through a retreating defensive line after a set restart had given the Warriors momentum.

He continued to torment Newcastle's right edge throughout the opening half, producing a brutal fend on Sandon Smith before breaking into space. Only a forward pass on the final exchange prevented the Warriors from turning the opportunity into more points.

With New Zealand's season rapidly slipping away, Halasima delivered again in the 70th minute, surging over for his second try and reducing Newcastle's lead to two.

The conversion attempt sailed wide, leaving the Warriors needing another score, but Halasima's performance offered a glimpse of what their attack could increasingly be built around.

He had spent much of the season establishing himself as one of the competition's most destructive young forwards. On Sunday, despite the hamstring concern and a positional switch, he showed he can be equally damaging when given room on an edge.

The concern for Andrew Webster will be how isolated that threat often appeared.

Outside of Halasima's individual power, the Warriors struggled to consistently create space or manipulate Newcastle's defensive line. Their other apparent second-half try, to Ali Leiataua, was correctly overturned for an obstruction.

Halasima nearly carried them across the line, but in a sudden-death final, nearly was not enough.

The Warriors saved their errors for the biggest moments
Finals football rarely demands perfection. It does, however, punish carelessness.

The Warriors learned that lesson in brutal fashion.

They had chances to take control of this contest but repeatedly released the pressure through an error, a mistimed pass or a poor decision.

The most costly arrived immediately after half-time.

With the scores locked at 6-6, Watene-Zelezniak attempted an offload under pressure and instead passed the ball directly to Bradman Best. Newcastle capitalised just a couple of plays later, shifting right for Dominic Young to score the try that ultimately decided the match.

It was far from the Warriors' only missed opportunity.

A promising first-half break from Halasima ended with a forward pass. Kurt Capewell followed a superb tackle on Young and a powerful carry with an error. Leiataua's second-half effort was erased by an obstruction, while several attacking sets close to Newcastle's line ended without the composure required to convert pressure into points.

Individually, none of those moments had to be fatal. Together, they told the story of a side that tightened up when its season was on the line.

It continued a worrying trend from the previous week. The Warriors had led the Dolphins 16-8 after an hour before conceding 18 unanswered points. Given a second opportunity at home, they again failed to close out a match they had every chance to win.

That makes this exit particularly painful.

New Zealand finished second and earned two home finals, yet their season ends with consecutive defeats and the sense that their best football deserted them at precisely the wrong time.

The Warriors' rise under Webster remains significant, while players such as Halasima provide ample reason for optimism. But the next stage of their development must be learning how to regain control when a finals match becomes frantic.

The premiership contenders still standing know how to make those moments feel routine.

For the second straight week, the Warriors made them feel overwhelming.
